\label{lemma-localize}
In Situation \ref{situation-global}.
Let $X' \subset X$ and $S' \subset S$ be open subschemes such that
$X'$ maps into $S'$. Then there is a fully faithful functor
$\text{Cris}(X'/S') \to \text{Cris}(X/S)$
which gives rise to a morphism of topoi fitting into the commutative
diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
(X'/S')_{\text{cris}} \ar[r] \ar[d]_{u_{X'/S'}} &
(X/S)_{\text{cris}} \ar[d]^{u_{X/S}} \\
\Sh(X'_{Zar}) \ar[r] & \Sh(X_{Zar})
}
$$
Moreover, this diagram is an example of localization of morphisms of
topoi as in Sites, Lemma \ref{sites-lemma-localize-morphism-topoi}.

With notation $X/S, \mathcal{I}, \gamma, \mathcal{C}, \mathcal{F}$
as in Definition \ref{definition-modules}. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is quasi-coherent, and
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is locally quasi-coherent and a crystal in
$\mathcal{O}_{X/S}$-modules.
\end{enumerate}
statement:
Fix a prime $p$ and a divided power scheme $(S,\mathcal I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, where $\mathcal I$ is a quasi-coherent ideal with divided powers. Set $S_0=V(\mathcal I)$ and choose a morphism $X\to S_0$ on which $p$ is locally nilpotent. A divided power thickening of $X/S$ is a triple $(U,T,\delta)$ with a closed immersion $U\hookrightarrow T$ inducing a homeomorphism on topological spaces, divided powers $\delta$ on its ideal $\mathcal J_T$, a compatible morphism of divided power schemes $T\to S$, and a map $U\to X$. These objects with compatible maps form $\mathrm{CRIS}(X/S)$; its full subcategory $\mathrm{Cris}(X/S)$ has $U\to X$ an open immersion. Both carry the Zariski topology (covers arise from Zariski covers of $T$ compatible with $U$). The forgetful functor $\mathrm{CRIS}(X/S)\to\operatorname{Sch}/X$ sends $(U,T,\delta)$ to $U$.

On the small crystalline site $\mathrm{Cris}(X/S)$, the crystalline structure sheaf $\mathcal O_{X/S}$ restricts to $\mathcal O_T$ on an object $(U,T,\delta)$. A sheaf $\mathcal F$ of $\mathcal O_{X/S}$-modules restricts to a sheaf $\mathcal F_T$ on $T$. It is a crystal if each pullback comparison map $f^*\mathcal F_T\to\mathcal F_{T'}$ for a morphism $(U',T',\delta')\to(U,T,\delta)$ is an isomorphism. It is locally quasi-coherent if every $\mathcal F_T$ is quasi-coherent, and quasi-coherent as a module on the site if it is locally presented by free $\mathcal O_{X/S}$-modules. The sheaf $\Omega_{X/S}$ is the universal divided power sheaf of differentials for the structure morphism of the crystalline site to the Zariski site of $S$; it restricts to $\Omega_{T/S,\delta}$ on each object.

Under the global crystalline setup above, let $\mathcal C=\mathrm{Cris}(X/S)$ or $\mathrm{CRIS}(X/S)$, and let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal O_{X/S}$-modules on $\mathcal C$. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is quasi-coherent, and
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is locally quasi-coherent and a crystal in
$\mathcal{O}_{X/S}$-modules.
\end{enumerate}

If an object $Y$ receives a map from every object and finite products exist, the augmented Cech complex of $Y$ has degree-$n$ terms $\mathcal F(Y^{n+1})$, with the coface maps induced by omission of factors. The derived global sections of an abelian sheaf are represented by this complex when the resulting Cech terms are acyclic.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category endowed with the chaotic topology.
Let $X$ be an object of $\mathcal{C}$ such that every object of
$\mathcal{C}$ has a morphism towards $X$. Assume that $\mathcal{C}$
has products of pairs.
Then for every abelian sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathcal{C}$
the total cohomology $R\Gamma(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{F})$ is represented
by the complex
$$
\mathcal{F}(X) \to \mathcal{F}(X \times X) \to
\mathcal{F}(X \times X \times X) \to \ldots
$$
associated to the cosimplicial abelian group $[n] \mapsto \mathcal{F}(X^{n+1})$.

A divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ is a commutative ring $A$, ideal $I$, and operations $\gamma_n:I\to I$ ($n\ge1$), with $\gamma_0(x)=1$, $\gamma_1(x)=x$, $\gamma_n(ax)=a^n\gamma_n(x)$, $\gamma_n(x+y)=\sum_{i+j=n}\gamma_i(x)\gamma_j(y)$, $\gamma_m(x)\gamma_n(x)=\binom{m+n}{m}\gamma_{m+n}(x)$, and $\gamma_m(\gamma_n(x))=(mn)!/(m!(n!)^m)\,\gamma_{mn}(x)$. A homomorphism of divided power rings carries distinguished ideals into one another and commutes with all divided power operations.

A divided power polynomial algebra $B\langle x_i\rangle$ over a divided power ring $(B,I,\delta)$ is freely generated by the divided power variables $x_i$, with ideal $IB\langle x_i\rangle+B\langle x_i\rangle_+$. \label{lemma-relative-poincare}
Let $A$ be a ring. Let $(B, I, \delta)$ be a divided power ring
where $B$ is an $A$-algebra.
Let $P = B\langle x_i \rangle$ be a divided power polynomial
ring over $B$ with divided power ideal $J = IP + B\langle x_i \rangle_{+}$
as usual. Let $M$ be a $B$-module endowed with an integrable connection
$\nabla : M \to M \otimes_B \Omega^1_{B/A, \delta}$. Then the map of
de Rham complexes
$$
M \otimes_B \Omega^*_{B/A, \delta}
\longrightarrow
M \otimes_P \Omega^*_{P/A, \delta}
$$
is a quasi-isomorphism. Let $D$, resp.\ $D'$ be the $p$-adic completion of
$B$, resp.\ $P$ and let $\Omega^i_D$, resp.\ $\Omega^i_{D'}$ be the $p$-adic
completion of $\Omega^i_{B/A, \delta}$,
resp.\ $\Omega^i_{P/A, \delta}$. Let $M$ be a $p$-adically complete
$D$-module endowed with an integral connection
$\nabla : M \to M \otimes^\wedge_D \Omega^1_D$.
Then the map of de Rham complexes
$$
M \otimes^\wedge_D \Omega^*_D
\longrightarrow
M \otimes^\wedge_D \Omega^*_{D'}
$$
is a quasi-isomorphism.

A divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ is a commutative ring $A$, ideal $I$, and operations $\gamma_n:I\to I$ ($n\ge1$), with $\gamma_0(x)=1$, $\gamma_1(x)=x$, $\gamma_n(ax)=a^n\gamma_n(x)$, $\gamma_n(x+y)=\sum_{i+j=n}\gamma_i(x)\gamma_j(y)$, $\gamma_m(x)\gamma_n(x)=\binom{m+n}{m}\gamma_{m+n}(x)$, and $\gamma_m(\gamma_n(x))=(mn)!/(m!(n!)^m)\,\gamma_{mn}(x)$. A homomorphism of divided power rings carries distinguished ideals into one another and commutes with all divided power operations.

Fix a prime $p$ and a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ with $A$ a $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$-algebra, together with an $A$-algebra $C$ such that $IC=0$ and $p$ is nilpotent in $C$. An object of $\mathrm{CRIS}(C/A)$ is a divided power $(A,I,\gamma)$-algebra $(B,J_B,\delta)$ with $p$ nilpotent in $B$ and a compatible $A$-algebra map $C\to B/J_B$; morphisms preserve the divided powers and this map from $C$. The full subcategory $\mathrm{Cris}(C/A)$ consists of objects with $C\cong B/J_B$. The completed category $\mathrm{Cris}^{\wedge}(C/A)$ has analogously compatible objects complete for the $p$-adic topology, with divided powers extended to the completion; for sufficiently large $e$, reductions $B/p^eB$ lie in $\mathrm{Cris}(C/A)$.

Fix a prime $p$ and a divided power scheme $(S,\mathcal I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, where $\mathcal I$ is a quasi-coherent ideal with divided powers. Set $S_0=V(\mathcal I)$ and choose a morphism $X\to S_0$ on which $p$ is locally nilpotent. A divided power thickening of $X/S$ is a triple $(U,T,\delta)$ with a closed immersion $U\hookrightarrow T$ inducing a homeomorphism on topological spaces, divided powers $\delta$ on its ideal $\mathcal J_T$, a compatible morphism of divided power schemes $T\to S$, and a map $U\to X$. These objects with compatible maps form $\mathrm{CRIS}(X/S)$; its full subcategory $\mathrm{Cris}(X/S)$ has $U\to X$ an open immersion. Both carry the Zariski topology (covers arise from Zariski covers of $T$ compatible with $U$). The forgetful functor $\mathrm{CRIS}(X/S)\to\operatorname{Sch}/X$ sends $(U,T,\delta)$ to $U$.

On the small crystalline site $\mathrm{Cris}(X/S)$, the crystalline structure sheaf $\mathcal O_{X/S}$ restricts to $\mathcal O_T$ on an object $(U,T,\delta)$. A sheaf $\mathcal F$ of $\mathcal O_{X/S}$-modules restricts to a sheaf $\mathcal F_T$ on $T$. It is a crystal if each pullback comparison map $f^*\mathcal F_T\to\mathcal F_{T'}$ for a morphism $(U',T',\delta')\to(U,T,\delta)$ is an isomorphism. It is locally quasi-coherent if every $\mathcal F_T$ is quasi-coherent, and quasi-coherent as a module on the site if it is locally presented by free $\mathcal O_{X/S}$-modules. The sheaf $\Omega_{X/S}$ is the universal divided power sheaf of differentials for the structure morphism of the crystalline site to the Zariski site of $S$; it restricts to $\Omega_{T/S,\delta}$ on each object.

scheme over $\mathbf{Z}_{(p)}$ with $p \in \mathcal{I}$. We set

statement:
Fix a prime $p$ and a divided power scheme $(S,\mathcal I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, where $\mathcal I$ is a quasi-coherent ideal with divided powers. Set $S_0=V(\mathcal I)$ and choose a morphism $X\to S_0$ on which $p$ is locally nilpotent. A divided power thickening of $X/S$ is a triple $(U,T,\delta)$ with a closed immersion $U\hookrightarrow T$ inducing a homeomorphism on topological spaces, divided powers $\delta$ on its ideal $\mathcal J_T$, a compatible morphism of divided power schemes $T\to S$, and a map $U\to X$. These objects with compatible maps form $\mathrm{CRIS}(X/S)$; its full subcategory $\mathrm{Cris}(X/S)$ has $U\to X$ an open immersion. Both carry the Zariski topology (covers arise from Zariski covers of $T$ compatible with $U$). The forgetful functor $\mathrm{CRIS}(X/S)\to\operatorname{Sch}/X$ sends $(U,T,\delta)$ to $U$.

On the small crystalline site $\mathrm{Cris}(X/S)$, the crystalline structure sheaf $\mathcal O_{X/S}$ restricts to $\mathcal O_T$ on an object $(U,T,\delta)$. A sheaf $\mathcal F$ of $\mathcal O_{X/S}$-modules restricts to a sheaf $\mathcal F_T$ on $T$. It is a crystal if each pullback comparison map $f^*\mathcal F_T\to\mathcal F_{T'}$ for a morphism $(U',T',\delta')\to(U,T,\delta)$ is an isomorphism. It is locally quasi-coherent if every $\mathcal F_T$ is quasi-coherent, and quasi-coherent as a module on the site if it is locally presented by free $\mathcal O_{X/S}$-modules. The sheaf $\Omega_{X/S}$ is the universal divided power sheaf of differentials for the structure morphism of the crystalline site to the Zariski site of $S$; it restricts to $\Omega_{T/S,\delta}$ on each object.

On the small crystalline site $\mathrm{Cris}(X/S)$, the universal divided-power derivation $d:\mathcal O_{X/S}\to\Omega^1_{X/S}$ extends to a de Rham complex $\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}$ with $\Omega^i_{X/S}=\wedge^i_{\mathcal O_{X/S}}\Omega^1_{X/S}$. For a crystal $\mathcal F$ of quasi-coherent modules, its canonical integrable connection $\nabla$ defines $\mathcal F\otimes\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}$. Let $u_{X/S}:(X/S)_{\mathrm{cris}}\to \operatorname{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{Zar}})$ be the canonical morphism of topoi induced by $(U,T,\delta)\mapsto U$, with right-derived pushforward $Ru_{X/S,*}$.

In characteristic $p$, an $\alpha_p$-cover is locally of the form $\operatorname{Spec}(C[z]/(z^p-c))\to\operatorname{Spec}C$, $c\in C$. An iterated $\alpha_p$-cover is, locally on the target, a composition of finitely many such covers. Such a cover is finite locally free and radicial, with locally constant degree a power of $p$; assume the degree is the fixed integer $q$. For the morphism of small crystalline topoi $f_{\mathrm{cris}}$, $f_{\mathrm{cris}}^*$ denotes pullback of crystals, and for $f:X'\to X$, $f_*$ denotes pushforward of sheaves on the underlying Zariski sites. A distinguished triangle $A\to B\to E\to A[1]$ in the derived category means that $E$ is a cone of the first morphism.
